title: Design Thinking: Why Half My Process Happens Before the First Idea

Bias toward doing and making over thinking and meeting.” – d.school Press enter or click to view image in full size Every great product starts with one belief: you matter. Half my design process is over before anyone is allowed to have an idea. 25% empathy. 25% problem definition. Only then do we touch a whiteboard. Ideation, the sticky-note part everyone loves? It gets 15%. Sounds backwards. It’s the one habit that stops my teams from building the wrong thing. Most teams do the opposite: a solution in meeting one, six months of build, and zero users who asked for it. That’s how you burn a quarter. Here’s my playbook: five steps, plus the one most frameworks forget. Press enter or click to view image in full size The 5 + 1 at a glance Empathy (25%): understand the humans. Define (25%): nail one sharp problem. Ideate (15%): go wide, then converge. Prototype (20%): make it real, cheap and fast. Test (15%): put it in users’ hands and learn. -- -- Written by Praveen Joshi 60 followers · 44 following Gen AI consultant, Auditing and Architecture Help Status About Careers Press Blog Store Privacy Rules Terms Text to speech
